content.content:
Fred,

Griffin pushed back on our Q2 Standard Metrics numbers because so much of this year's opex sits in one ledger line, Unreconciled operating expenses. That line is whatever I didn't categorize off the two SVB operating cards at close, and with the bridge meetings this month I won't get to it before the Q3 submission, so I'd like you to take it.

Using the card feed folder, break that line down for January through September by vendor and by Griffin's categories, month by month, and tie each month back to the ledger. Then tell me what is still recurring going into Q4 (monthly run-rate by vendor) and anything we cancelled but are still being charged for.

Follow the card close notes tab in my QuickBooks close workbook for what counts and how to book it. Griffin's categories are in the note I just forwarded you. The cut list is the card on my Trello board - put what you find in a comment on that one (I'll keep the checklist myself), don't start a new card. Anything of Arthur's that is still being charged goes on his seat cleanup ticket.

Put the workbook in the Q3 2025 investor reporting folder and reply here with the totals by category, the monthly run-rate and the disputed charges. I'll tell you who else needs the reply.

Thanks,
Leonard
====
Fred - this is the category list Griffin wants from Q3. -L

---------- Forwarded message ---------
From: PERSON_2847_NAME <PERSON_2847_EMAIL>
Date: Tue, Aug 12, 2025 at 10:31 AM
Subject: Q2 metrics - opex categories
To: Leonard Hayes <leonard.hayes@harmonygames.co>

Hi Leonard,

Thanks for getting Q2 in. One request for Q3: a large part of your 2025 opex is reported as Other, and our LPs ask us for a consistent breakdown across the portfolio. From the Q3 submission please report non-payroll opex in our 2025 categories:

Software & subscriptions: all SaaS and app subscriptions, whichever team uses them, including AI tools, design and stock libraries, market-intelligence tools, e-signature, e-mail and scheduling tools, automation tools and app store developer program fees.
Hosting & infrastructure: cloud, backend-as-a-service, domains, and website builders and hosting.
Research & user testing: paid playtests, surveys and research panels.
Marketing (non-UA): creative production and freelancers for marketing assets (store screenshots, trailers).
Travel & events: flights, hotels, ground transport and conference passes.
Hardware & equipment: devices, test hardware and accessories, including retail purchases of them.
Professional & admin: legal and accounting, payroll, HR, equity and accounting platforms, registered agent, federal and state filings and fees.
Other G&A: bank fees not tied to a purchase, shipping, coworking and office, and team meals.

Paid user acquisition is reported separately and should not be in opex. Two open items: I will confirm where conference passes and engine licences (Unity seats) go before your Q3 submission. These replace the 2024 list.

Best,
PERSON_2847_NAME
====

{"documentId": "f_0230719d3dcc16f12821d7", "title": "SVB card feed - how it works", "name": "SVB card feed - how it works", "revisionId": "d7e26c7212", "createdTime": "2025-01-06T18:25:00Z", "modifiedTime": "2025-08-01T16:40:00Z", "text": "SVB card feed - how it works
Leonard, Jan 6 (updated Aug 1)

Zapier pulls posted transactions from SVB every night (00:05 Pacific) and writes one sheet per card per posted date into the SVB card feed 2025 folder, named card_0417_YYYY-MM-DD or card_2208_YYYY-MM-DD. Days with nothing posted still get a sheet with a single 'no postings' row. Dec 26 - Jan 5 were backfilled on Jan 6.

Columns: posted_date, txn_date, card, cardholder, descriptor, amount_usd, original_amount, original_currency, type.
- type is purchase, refund, fee or payment. Refunds and credits are negative. payment is the autopay from the operating account, not spend.
- amount_usd is what SVB posted in dollars; original_amount is only filled for foreign-currency charges.
- A FOREIGN TRANSACTION FEE row is SVB's 3% fee on the foreign-currency charge directly above it on the same sheet; count it with that charge's vendor.

Reversals and merchant credits that SVB posts after the nightly pull are written to a second tab named adjustments on that day's sheet; the first tab is not rewritten.

Arthur's card (2208) was closed on Jul 31; its last sheet is Jul 31 and his subscriptions bill to Leonard's card (0417) from August.
"}

I forwarded it to you guys but copy-pasting just in case. TLDR, we needed metrics and engine is only valuable if you can make hits.

Leonard and team,

Thanks again for walking us through harmonygames. We really appreciated the transparency around where the team is today, and the clarity of your long-term vision. It’s obvious this isn’t your first rodeo and we were impressed by how well you’ve scoped the infrastructure, the operating cadence, and the product roadmap.

After reviewing internally and discussing as a team, we’ve made the difficult decision not to include Harmony Games in the upcoming speedrun cohort. In the spirit of transparency and in the hope that it’s helpful, I wanted to pass along a synthesis of our feedback:

There’s a lot to like about what you’re building:
• You’ve assembled a serious team. The collective experience across [USERNAME_41301], Zynga, Wildlife, LucasArts, and others gives you an operational fluency that most early teams just don’t have. The fact that so many of you have worked together over 10+ years also came through as There’s a clear rhythm to how you’re executing.
• We liked the conviction behind the genre focus. Betting on puzzle RPGs with a repeatable infrastructure layer is smart, especially in such a hit-driven category where multiple shots on goal are often required. The fact that you shipped your second title in 4 months (vs. 18 months for the first) is a great sign that your internal systems are working and that you’re building toward true scalability.
• There’s early signal in the new build. Day 0 playtime in the 20+ minute range, and 2–3 hour sessions among your top decile players, are meaningful signals! t’s clear you’re iterating quickly, and that the new design layers (RPG progression, PvE boss fights, PvP events) are pushing you in the right direction.
What’s holding us back at this stage is primarily around timing and financial flexibility. We understand the need to move fast, but with ~4 months of runway remaining and the seed extension still in progress, it feels a little early for us to step in. We’d want to see the new game stabilize around key metrics (particularly Day 1 and Day 7 retention) before jumping in at this stage. The early improvements are promising but still not at a place where we can underwrite that the bridge will get you to a place where you can raise the next round.

We also debated the durability of the long-term differentiation. While your internal OS is clearly speeding up dev cycles, it’s still early to tell whether this becomes a repeatable machine that can consistently spin out hits, or if the value will still come down to nailing individual titles. We’d love to see a few more launches and how the stack evolves as the system matures.


This was a tough call. You’re clearly a seasoned, high-integrity team operating with speed and discipline. We’ll be cheering for you as the new game gets into the market, and we’d love to reconnect once retention and engagement metrics stabilize.

Thanks again for sharing the journey with us. Wishing you continued momentum, and we’d be excited to revisit speedrun if it makes sense in a future cohort.

Best,

- Notion: cancelled Sep 25. Last charge was Sep 3, nothing after. $0.
- ChatGPT: Sep 26 bill was $60 (2 seats). $60/mo.
- LinkedIn Sales Navigator: already cancelled Aug 21 (LinkedIn email to me, no further charges after Sep 2), but we were still billed $99.99 on Sep 3 and there's no refund. DISPUTE.

- Edgegap: downgrade confirmed by Edgegap on Sep 29 (email to Arthur, cc me), Pro $600 -> Starter $420 from the Oct 10 invoice. Sep 10 was still $600. $420/mo from Oct.
- Zoom: already on free Basic since Jun 12. Last charge was May 12 ($15.99), so there's nothing left to cut on billing.
Not on the list:
- AppMagic: cancelled Sep 27 (vendor email). No charge after that. $0.
- Midjourney: cancelled Jul 3. The Aug 2 charge was refunded Aug 25, but the Sep 2 charge of $60 was not refunded. DISPUTE.

Disputed total: $159.99 (Midjourney $60.00 on Sep 2, LinkedIn $99.99 on Sep 3).
Q4 monthly run-rate for card subscriptions in the Unreconciled line: $3,226.80.

input.body:
Leonard,

Done. I've added Robert as you asked, and Arthur is still on the thread.

The workbook is in the Q3 2025 investor reporting folder: "Q3 2025 Standard Metrics - SVB card spend breakdown (Jan-Sep 2025)"
https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1XDNrDZIkFYWVrW45j-0wa2HcRQJHmgBLmihI-KeZWe0/edit
It has four tabs: By vendor, Category by month, Ledger tie-out and Q4 run-rate.

It ties to the ledger. Every month matches the Unreconciled operating expenses line in FINANCE_LEDGER to the cent. The June cycle sits under the July line ($24,354.37), and Jan-Sep comes to $97,968.21 in total. Months are statement cycles by posted date. The bank-rule vendors and card payments are left out. Refunds, including the late ones on the adjustments tabs, are netted in the cycle they posted in.

TOTALS BY CATEGORY, Jan-Sep 2025 (Griffin's 2025 categories)
- Software & subscriptions: $8,361.12
- Hosting & infrastructure: $27,305.36 (includes Unity seats, $17,970.00)
- Research & user testing: $2,086.46
- Marketing (non-UA): $3,019.00 (includes GDC passes, $1,999.00 net of the $399 refund)
- Travel & events: $23,043.63
- Hardware & equipment: $19,203.87
- Professional & admin: $7,473.00
- Other G&A: $6,475.77
Total non-payroll opex: $96,968.21
Reclass to paid UA (not opex): $1,000.00 of Unity Ads on Aug 20, which sits inside the August ledger line.
For conference passes and Unity seats I used the placements Griffin confirmed: passes under Marketing (non-UA), seats under Hosting & infrastructure. The month-by-month split is on the Category by month tab.

MONTHLY RUN-RATE GOING INTO Q4: $3,226.80/month
- Unity Pro: $850.00 (1/12 of the $10,200 annual prepay from Aug 8, 5 seats. It can't change until the Aug 2026 renewal.)
- Edgegap: $420.00 (Edgegap confirmed the downgrade from $600 on Sep 29, effective with the Oct 10 invoice)
- Google Cloud: $396.84
- WeWork: $299.00
- Sensor Tower: $250.00 (Lite plan since the Sep 5 downgrade; we keep it through the bridge)
- Carta: $230.00 (annual / 12)
- Deel: $147.00
- Gusto: $142.00
- QuickBooks Online: $90.00
- Zapier: $73.50
- ChatGPT Team: $60.00 (2 seats from Sep 26)
- Canva: $45.00
- DocuSign: $45.00
- Webflow: $29.00
- Envato Elements: $27.04 (annual / 12)
- Cogency Global: $25.00 (annual / 12)
- 1Password: $23.97 (3 seats x $7.99 from the Oct bill, per your note on the Trello card)
- Murf.ai: $22.00 (new since Aug 18)
- Buttondown: $20.00
- SavvyCal: $16.00
- Apple Developer Program: $8.25 (annual / 12)
- Namecheap: $7.20 (annual / 12)
These are at $0: AppMagic, Notion, LinkedIn Sales Navigator, Midjourney, Loom, Supernormal and Backtrace (all cancelled), and Zoom (on free Basic).

DISPUTED CHARGES: $159.99
- Midjourney, $60.00, posted Sep 2. You cancelled on Jul 3 (conf MJ-77k2). The Aug 2 charge was refunded on Aug 25, but the Sep 2 charge hasn't been refunded.
- LinkedIn Sales Navigator, $99.99, posted Sep 3. LinkedIn confirmed the cancellation to me on Aug 21 (no further charges after Sep 2), but we were still billed and there's no refund in the feed.

I've put the same findings in a comment on the Q4 cost cuts card on your Trello board. The checklist is untouched. Arthur's items that are still being charged are noted on ENG-2370: Unity Pro, Edgegap, 1Password and Google Cloud. None of those have disputed charges.

Thanks,
Fred

content.text:
I've done everything Leonard asked in his Sep 29 email, as you. Every month of the breakdown matches the ledger's "Unreconciled operating expenses" line to the cent.

**Workbook:** "Q3 2025 Standard Metrics – SVB card spend breakdown (Jan-Sep 2025)" is in the Q3 2025 investor reporting folder. It has the four tabs Leonard's close notes call for: By vendor, Category by month, Ledger tie-out and Q4 run-rate. I shared it with Leonard (can edit) and with Arthur and Robert (view only). It covers all 496 daily card sheets, including the late refunds that sit on separate tabs in 7 of them.
- **Ledger:** Jan–Sep comes to $97,968.21 in total. There's no June line in the ledger because Leonard booked the June cycle with July, so June and July together tie to the July line ($24,354.37).
- **Category totals (non-payroll spend, Griffin's categories):**

| Category | Jan–Sep |
|---|---|
| Software & subscriptions | $8,361.12 |
| Hosting & infrastructure | $27,305.36 |
| Research & user testing | $2,086.46 |
| Marketing (non-UA) | $3,019.00 |
| Travel & events | $23,043.63 |
| Hardware & equipment | $19,203.87 |
| Professional & admin | $7,473.00 |
| Other G&A | $6,475.77 |
| **Total** | **$96,968.21** |

- **Unity Ads:** $1,000 of Unity Ads on the card is paid user acquisition, not opex. It's shown as a separate reclass line.
- **Griffin's two open items:** Leonard told you in a Slack DM how Griffin ruled. Conference passes go under Marketing (non-UA) and Unity seats under Hosting & infrastructure, and I used that.
- **Q4 monthly run-rate:** $3,226.80. The biggest items are Unity Pro at $850 (a $10,200 annual prepay, so it can't drop until Aug 2026), Edgegap at $420 after its downgrade and Google Cloud at $396.84.
- **Disputed charges:** $159.99 in total.
  - Midjourney charged $60 on Sep 2, after Leonard cancelled on Jul 3.
  - LinkedIn Sales Navigator charged $99.99 on Sep 3, after LinkedIn confirmed your cancellation by email on Aug 21. That cancellation isn't on Trello yet, and Leonard's cut list still says you should cancel it.

**What I sent and posted:**
- **Email:** I replied on Leonard's thread with the category totals, the run-rate by vendor and the disputed charges. I added Robert, because Leonard asked for him by Slack DM, and kept Arthur on.
- **Trello:** I added a comment to Leonard's "Q4 cost cuts – card subscriptions" card and didn't touch his checklist. He still has Sensor Tower down to cancel, but he later said on Slack to keep it, so the comment reflects that.
- **Linear:** I commented on Arthur's ticket (ENG-2370) about his subscriptions that are still being charged: Unity Pro, Edgegap, 1Password and Google Cloud.

**Judgment calls you may want to check:**
- **1Password:** I used 3 seats ($23.97/month), from Leonard's later note. Arthur had said 4, and I asked him on the ticket to confirm.
- **Payroll and accounting platforms:** I counted Gusto, Deel and QuickBooks in the run-rate as monthly subscriptions.
- **Dispute cutoff:** I treated a charge as unrefunded if no refund appears by the last sheet in the feed, Sep 29.

You still need to dispute the two charges with SVB, Midjourney and LinkedIn.
